title: SITA: Learning Speaker-Invariant and Tone-Aware Speech Representations for Low-Resource Tonal Languages
abstract: arXiv:2601.09050v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Tonal low-resource languages are widely spoken but remain underserved by modern speech technologies. A central challenge is learning speech representations that are robust to nuisance variation, such as speaker gender, while preserving lexical tone, which carries word meaning. We propose SITA, a lightweight adaptation recipe for pretrained wav2vec-style self-supervised speech encoders. Rather than designing a new backbone or objective, SITA combines existing objectives in a staged optimization framework to reduce tone collapse while preserving ASR capability. Stage 1 improves speaker invariance without erasing tonal contrasts by combining a cross-gender contrastive loss with a tone-repulsive loss that separates same-word, different-tone realizations. translated_title: SITA：面向低资源声调语言的说话人不变且声调感知的语音表示学习
translated_abstract: 低资源声调语言使用人数众多，但现代语音技术对其服务仍然不足。一个核心挑战是学习对说话人性别等干扰性变化具有鲁棒性的语音表示，同时保留承载词义的词汇声调。我们提出了SITA，这是一种针对预训练wav2vec风格自监督语音编码器的轻量级适配方案。SITA并未设计新的骨干网络或目标函数，而是在分阶段优化框架中组合现有目标函数，以减少声调塌缩，同时保持自动语音识别（ASR）能力。第一阶段通过将跨性别对比损失与声调排斥损失（用于区分同一词语的不同声调发音）相结合，在不抹除声调对立的情况下提升说话人不变性。第二阶段通过在上层编码器层进行CTC微调和知识蒸馏来恢复面向识别的语言信息。我们主要在苗语（一种声调语言）上评估SITA。
tldr: SITA提出一种轻量级两阶段适配方案，通过跨性别对比损失与声调排斥损失以及CTC微调，使wav2vec风格语音编码器在保持词汇声调与识别能力的同时获得说话人不变性，从而提升低资源声调语言（如苗语）的语音处理效果。
en_tdlr: SITA is a lightweight two-stage adaptation recipe that combines cross-gender contrastive loss, tone-repulsive loss, and CTC fine-tuning to make wav2vec-style speech encoders speaker-invariant while preserving lexical tone and ASR capability for low-resource tonal languages such as Hmong.
